# Everything after a -- is handed to go test as written, so mutants run the way
# the suite does: build tags, -race, -shuffle, whatever it needs.
#
# The only test that asserts on the rendered text is behind a build tag. Without
# the tag it does not exist, so the mutant survives; passed through, it reaches
# the mutant's run and catches it.

muxt test-template-mutations --seed 1
cmp stdout want-untagged.txt

muxt test-template-mutations --seed 1 -- -tags=extra
cmp stdout want-tagged.txt

# -overlay is refused: it is how each mutant reaches the build, and a second
# one would leave the run measuring templates nobody mutated.
! muxt test-template-mutations --seed 1 -- -overlay=mine.json
stderr 'go test flag -overlay cannot be passed through: muxt uses -overlay to deliver each mutant'

-- go.mod --
module server

go 1.24
-- templates.gohtml --
{{define "greeting"}}Hello, {{.Name}}!{{end}}
-- template.go --
package server

import (
	"embed"
	"html/template"
	"io"
)

//go:embed *.gohtml
var templateFiles embed.FS

var templates = template.Must(template.ParseFS(templateFiles, "*.gohtml"))

type Page struct {
	Name string
}

func Greet(w io.Writer, page Page) error {
	return templates.ExecuteTemplate(w, "greeting", page)
}
-- render_test.go --
package server

import (
	"strings"
	"testing"
)

func TestGreetRenders(t *testing.T) {
	var buf strings.Builder
	if err := Greet(&buf, Page{Name: "World"}); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
}
-- tagged_test.go --
//go:build extra

package server

import (
	"strings"
	"testing"
)

func TestGreetText(t *testing.T) {
	var buf strings.Builder
	if err := Greet(&buf, Page{Name: "World"}); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if got, want := buf.String(), "Hello, World!"; got != want {
		t.Errorf("greeting = %q, want %q", got, want)
	}
}
